turns.question: Where is the structural map engine implemented, and how is the parser engine selected per file?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the repository structure remotely using the gh CLI.Found `internal/mapengine/` directory. Let me read those files directly.Now let me check goast.go and regex.go, plus find where mapengine is invoked from CLI (the "map" command) and where `.ghxmap`/config might override engine selection.Now let's check where the CLI wires this up — the `map` command and how the `--engine` flag is exposed and passed through, plus grep for other callers.Found it — `internal/ghx/read.go` is the actual call site. Let me view the relevant sections of read.go and ghx.go for full context.I have a complete picture now. Let me also quickly check ADR-0013 for the documented design rationale to corroborate.This confirms the design (ADR-0013) matches the actual code exactly. Here's the full answer.

## Structural map engine location

**Package:** `internal/mapengine/` (Go, no CGo)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `internal/mapengine/types.go` | Shared `Mapper` interface, `Options`/`Result`/`Symbol` types, the `Map()` entry point, and the engine-routing logic (`mapAuto`, `mapTreeSitterWithFallback`) |
| `internal/mapengine/goast.go` | `GoASTMapper` — uses Go's stdlib `go/ast` + `go/parser` to extract packages, funcs, types, const/var decls from `.go` files |
| `internal/mapengine/treesitter.go` | `TreeSitterMapper` — uses the pure-Go `github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter` library (+ bundled `grammars`) with per-language `TreeSitterLanguageConfig` (tags query, tag→kind mapping, signature formatter) for TS/TSX/JS/Python/Rust |
| `internal/mapengine/regex.go` | `RegexMapper` — line-anchored regex rules per language extension (go, ts/tsx/js/jsx, py, rs, java, kt, rb); universal fallback engine |
| `internal/mapengine/regex_test.go` | Tests covering all three engines and the routing behavior |

The design and its rationale are documented in `docs/adr/0013-ghx-map-command.md`, whose "Engineering plan ✓ Done" section matches the code 1:1.

## How the parser engine is selected per file

Selection happens in `mapengine.Map()` (`internal/mapengine/types.go`), which is called from `internal/ghx/read.go:187` (used by `ghx read --map`, `ghx serve` MCP tool, and the codemode registry — all pass through this single call site, per ADR-0013 point 2).

`Map(path, content, opts)` switches on `opts.Engine`:

- **`EngineRegex`** → forces `RegexMapper{}.Map(...)` directly.
- **`EngineTreeSitter`** → forces tree-sitter via `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., warnUnsupported=true)`, which falls back to `RegexMapper` (with a warning) if tree-sitter errors (e.g. unsupported language).
- **`EngineAuto`** (default) → `mapAuto()` dispatches by file extension (`filepath.Ext(path)`, lowercased):
  - `.go` → `GoASTMapper{}.Map(...)`; on parse error falls back to `RegexMapper` (marked `Fallback: true`)
  - `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.py`, `.rs` → tree-sitter, again falling back to regex on failure
  - anything else → `RegexMapper{}.Map(...)` directly
- Any unrecognized/garbage `Engine` value → regex, flagged as a fallback with a warning.

Additionally, inside `TreeSitterMapper.Map`, language configs can set `MergeRegex: true` (true for go, typescript, tsx, javascript, python, rust configs) to merge in regex-detected symbols the tree-sitter grammar doesn't tag (e.g. Go `import`/`package`, Rust `use` statements) — so even the tree-sitter path uses `RegexMapper` as a supplementary pass, not just a failure fallback.

The `Engine` choice is user-controllable end-to-end: CLI flag `--map-engine` (`internal/cli/ghx.go:112`) and MCP tool parameter `mapEngine` (`internal/cli/serve.go:99,272`, `internal/ghx/register.go:68,137`) both thread a string (`auto|regex|tree-sitter`) into `ReadOpts.MapEngine` → `mapengine.Options.Engine`.

**Not verified:** I did not check `internal/codemode/*` or `internal/cli/code.go` for any additional call sites into `mapengine` (grep/search showed none, but I didn't exhaustively read those files), nor did I check test files beyond `regex_test.go` for engine-specific coverage, nor confirm behavior against the actual `gotreesitter`/`grammars` library internals (treated as external dependency).
